hypothesis: The two measured OpenMP variants use per-worker cutoffs of 512 and 256 options, with similar means and no per-size timings available. Requiring at least 1024 options per effective worker tests the contrasting assumption that a coarser grain avoids parallel overhead on medium workloads while retaining static-scheduled parallelism for large workloads. The controller should compare the resulting serial/parallel boundary against the baseline and earlier variants; no gain is assumed.
notes: The catalog has two distinct measured source programs, both valid; the 256-options-per-effective-worker candidate is slightly faster in aggregate than the other candidate, but no per-case timings are supplied. This candidate uses a generic per-effective-worker cutoff of 1024, so at the observed four-thread cases n=16, 128, and 1024 remain serial while n=131072 uses static OpenMP scheduling. Each parallel iteration writes its unique result index; the team request is bounded by min(threads,n), and the nested-parallel guard avoids creating a nested team. No commands or measurements were run here; the controller must verify correctness and measure overhead and gains under the frozen protocol.
